newsitem.title: USA: Commonwealth Edison sets program on NRC concerns.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth Edison sets program on NRC concerns.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co, a unit of Unicom Corp, on Monday outlined steps it plans to take to address the Nuclear Regulatory Commisson's concerns about operations at six nuclear power plants.

In a 60-page letter sent in response to the NRC, the utility said it will improve oversight and standardize procedures at the facilities, rigorously enforce performance standards and increase resources for its Nuclear Division.
In January, the NRC wanted the utility to explain why it should be allowed to operate its nuclear plants while addressing operating problems at the facilities.
The utility responded at the time by increasing its budget for expenditures for the nuclear operation by 11 percent to $1.028 billion.
ComEd said its latest letter to the NRC details more than 200 specific site actions to upgrade engineering and technical support throughout the nuclear plant subsidiary.
Additionally, the company said Andrew Lynch will join the division as a vice president in charge of financial and administrative services, effective April 1.
Com Ed provides electrical service to about 3.4 million customers in northern Illinois.
Unicom shares were off 5/8 Monday at 19-3/4.
